recordDecisions.title: An $n^{0.3+\varepsilon}$-Approximation for Steiner $k$-Forest
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: The paper reports an n^(0.3+epsilon)-approximation for general Steiner k-Forest for every constant epsilon>0, improving the longstanding square-root-in-n general-case and n^0.448 uniform-weight bounds. It separately gives a conditional Densest-k-Subgraph/Sum-of-Squares barrier to improving the square-root-in-k dependence.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The author reports that ChatGPT suggested tree embeddings for k-MST, inspiring their use for Steiner k-Forest, and supplied the height-reduction reference used in Lemma 2.2. The author expressly prohibited further model research ideas; later assistance was editorial. Do not attribute the full algorithm or proof to ChatGPT.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Check whether this disclosed strategy/reference suggestion was materially essential to the algorithm, independently verify the approximation exponent and explicit parameter restrictions, and keep the k-dependence obstruction conditional rather than an unconditional hardness theorem. Confirm the exact first-public announcement date and that the direct AI disclosure was present in v1; this record uses the first retained public qualifying snapshot on 8 October, not a submission timestamp as a verified publication date. No independent complete proof review or artifact replay was performed. Keep provisional=1, low taxonomy confidence, reviewStatus unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

recordDecisions.comparator: Material improvement of a longstanding general approximation exponent, not a complete optimal solution of Steiner k-Forest.

recordDecisions.title: Two-Variable Logic with Arbitrarily Many Successor Relations
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: The paper reports uniform 2NEXPTIME decidability of satisfiability and infinite satisfiability for two-variable first-order logic with an arbitrary finite input-dependent number of exact successor relations; arbitrary unary/binary predicates are permitted but the orders themselves are absent from the language. Finite satisfiability under a budget on lost reference adjacencies is NEXPTIME-complete.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The authors directly credit GPT-6 Astra with a complex proof argument based on their initial notes; they deconstructed, simplified, rewrote and checked nearly the whole proof. GPT-6.1 Sol also helped editing. This is author-directed shared proof development, not intervention-free autonomy.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Independently verify the finite certificates, recovery of exact successors for arbitrary order types, complexity uniformity and bounded-loss finite-model restriction; do not extend the 2NEXPTIME claim to unrestricted finite satisfiability or languages containing the orders. Confirm the exact first-public announcement date and that the direct AI disclosure was present in v1; this record uses the first retained public qualifying snapshot on 8 October, not a submission timestamp as a verified publication date. No independent complete proof review or artifact replay was performed. Keep provisional=1, low taxonomy confidence, reviewStatus unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

recordDecisions.title: Optimal (Parallel) Spooky Pebbling on Binary Trees
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: The paper reports asymptotically optimal work Theta(nh/log(s+1)) for spooky pebbling of the complete binary tree with n=2^h-1 and h+1<=s<=n, and matching optimal parallel depth Theta(h+(n/s) max{h/log(s+1),1+log-star(h)}). The minimum-space work becomes Theta(n log(n)/log log(n)), resolving the cited time-optimality question.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The paper says the lower-bound proofs were developed through iterative exchanges with GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol. The authors take responsibility. Model-assisted text, application searches and computational experiments are separate from this directly disclosed mathematical contribution.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Independently check both work and depth lower bounds, the complete-tree upper-bound domain and full-tree lower-bound domain, the space-budget convention and the optimality comparator. Do not confuse reported application gate-count experiments with a proof for all circuits. Confirm the exact first-public announcement date and that the direct AI disclosure was present in v1; this record uses the first retained public qualifying snapshot on 8 October, not a submission timestamp as a verified publication date. No independent complete proof review or artifact replay was performed. Keep provisional=1, low taxonomy confidence, reviewStatus unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

recordDecisions.title: Network Coding Can Beat Routing in Undirected Multiple-Unicast Networks
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: The paper reports a counterexample to the 2004 Li–Li conjecture: a finite connected simple undirected network with unit shared edge capacities, maximum degree three and distinct leaf terminals admits a binary linear block code with common rate strictly above fractional routing. It additionally reports unbounded simple subcubic bipartite high-girth families with coding rate approaching one and routing rate bounded by a negative power of log(n).
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The primary paper directly says GPT-6 Astra assisted in developing the mathematical proofs and Lean code. It reports standard-axiom formalizations of the finite counterexample and family theorem; this automation did not replay or inspect those artifacts.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Independently verify the shared-capacity communication convention, deterministic schedule/rate-region scope, strict routing bound and tensor amplification; replay the pinned formal development and establish exact paper/Lean correspondence. Author-reported standard axioms are not an independent kernel check. Confirm the exact first-public announcement date and that the direct AI disclosure was present in v1; this record uses the first retained public qualifying snapshot on 8 October, not a submission timestamp as a verified publication date. No independent complete proof review or artifact replay was performed. Keep provisional=1, low taxonomy confidence, reviewStatus unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.

recordDecisions.title: Separating comb inequalities is NP-hard
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: The paper reports NP-completeness of deciding whether a comb inequality is violated, hence NP-hardness of exact comb separation, even for vectors in the symmetric-TSP subtour elimination polytope with edge values 0, 1/2 or 1 and nonplanar maximum-degree-four support. The stated tooth-restricted variant is also hard.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The authors credit GPT-6 and Claude Fable 5.1 with proposed reductions, graph constructions, candidate proof arguments, computational checks and counterexample searches. The humans formulated the question, directed the work, checked the arguments and simplified the results.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Independently verify the 3-SAT reduction, gadget consistency, subtour feasibility and NP-membership witness encoding. Establish exact novelty/priority for unrestricted versus restricted comb separation. Do not infer hardness for larger inequality families merely from comb separation. Confirm the exact first-public announcement date and that the direct AI disclosure was present in v1; this record uses the first retained public qualifying snapshot on 8 October, not a submission timestamp as a verified publication date. recordDecisions.title: Equilibria of Inverse-Square Repulsion on the Line Are Arithmetic Progressions
recordDecisions.boundedClaim: The paper reports that any locally finite subset of the real line with at least two points, absolutely convergent total force at each point and zero net repulsive force for exponent 1<s<=2 is an arithmetic progression, without an extremal-gap assumption. In particular it reports a positive solution of Benjamini’s inverse-square equilibrium question.
recordDecisions.aiContribution: The author directly discloses AI-assisted problem identification, literature search, discovery of the proof and computational checks, and says the proofs and sources were reviewed by the author. The model identity and detailed allocation are not disclosed; material proof assistance is reported but autonomy is not established.
recordDecisions.furtherChecking: Independently check recurrence of the gap-harmonic Doob transform and the absolute-convergence/local-finiteness hypotheses, novelty against the 2017 extremal-gap result, and exact model contribution. The theorem does not cover exponents above two, general force laws or principal-value equilibria. Confirm the exact first-public announcement date and that the direct AI disclosure was present in v1; this record uses the first retained public qualifying snapshot on 8 October, not a submission timestamp as a verified publication date. No independent complete proof review or artifact replay was performed. Keep provisional=1, low taxonomy confidence, reviewStatus unreviewed and no strict Superhuman override.
